findings.where: First screen, the row of five outlined pills under the lead paragraph (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation), at desktop and phone
findings.fault: These are static labels, and clicking them does nothing. They look like filter chips or buttons: each has its own rounded outline and semibold UI type, they sit right next to the one action, and on the phone they look like tap targets. A visitor who taps 'PPP Law' expecting Mark's PPP articles gets nothing. That is a false affordance, and it puts five fake controls between the message and the address.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who wants Mark's PPP law work and taps the 'PPP Law' pill, and anyone who tries one and nothing happens. Either may decide the page is broken just before they reach the contact.

findings.where: First screen, the primary action: the white 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com →' button
findings.fault: The page's one action is a link to '#', so clicking it neither opens an email nor goes anywhere. The arrow also suggests a jump to another page rather than writing an email. The address is shown, but the action that should come with it does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor ready to get in touch who clicks the address, nothing happens, and they have to copy it by hand. Getting in touch is the page's job under brand sheet §1.

findings.where: Article specimen: the 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' link and the three list bullets above it, both orange-red; compare 'Play again' in the motion sketch, which is house blue
findings.fault: Links appear in two looks, blue and orange-red, and the page's own palette says links are house blue. The orange link colour is also used on the static list bullets. A reader can't learn one link colour, and the bullets borrow the colour that marks a link.
findings.who_objects: A reader on Angélique's article pages, who sees orange decoration and an orange link side by side, can't tell what can be clicked. Some of them will miss the PDF link at the end of the article.
